evidence.name: First contact with a newly registered domain
evidence.objective: Prove an organisation-wide novelty rule fires on first contact with a newly registered domain, which per-host novelty (REP-008) cannot see.

distributions.baseline: a stable set of synthetic domains, each queried once by one host, establishing organizational normal
distributions.novel: domains never queried before by any host, low query count, contacted by few hosts

evidence.benign_baseline: the baseline_domains phase IS the baseline. Novelty is organization-wide, unlike REP-008 which is novel per host
evidence.transferability_note: The organisation-wide first-contact novelty (a domain never queried before) transfers, but the cited PREDATOR-class detector scores domain registration age from WHOIS. The emitted domains use reserved TLDs and carry no registration metadata, and Replicant performs no WHOIS, so the registration-age scoring the shipped rule depends on is not exercised.
evidence.safety_notes: novel domains use reserved TLDs. Replicant performs no registration and no WHOIS lookup, and resolves nothing
